text: Flutter 'Failed to build iOS app' under Xcode 16 is an umbrella for six different bugs. The umbrella message only tells you xcodebuild exited non-zero. Run with --verbose, grep for the first lowercase 'error:', and fix that. The four most common root causes: Flutter older than 3.24.4, Podfile still pinning iOS 11, a stale Pods plus DerivedData ModuleCache from the previous Xcode, or a plugin that hasn't shipped a Swift 6 release yet. Stop reaching for flutter clean first; it does not touch the iOS caches that are actually broken.

.NET 10's SDK flips two defaults at once: RestoreEnablePackagePruning=true and NuGetAuditMode=all. The runtime ships System.Text.Json, System.Formats.Asn1 and friends already, so listing them in the transitive graph just generated phantom CVEs in dotnet list package --vulnerable. New NU1510 warning fires when a direct PackageReference is fully redundant.

EF Core 11 vs Dapper for bulk inserts, real numbers: at 1M rows EF AddRange takes 21.6 s, Dapper ExecuteAsync 109 s, SqlBulkCopy 7.3 s. Use AddRange under 1,000 rows, SqlBulkCopy (or EFCore.BulkExtensions) above 10,000. Dapper is a full order of magnitude slower than EF for bulk because it has no row batching.

ConfigureAwait(false) in .NET 11: a no-op in ASP.NET Core, console apps, generic-host workers, and async Task xUnit tests, because none of them install a SynchronizationContext. Library code that ships as NuGet or multi-targets netstandard2.0 still needs it on every await, or a caller on WinForms or MAUI will deadlock on .Result.

Aider treats your git repo as the universe and /add /etc/nginx.conf returns 'not in the git repository'. Five working patterns for editing or reading external files: pass paths at launch (the CLI is more permissive than /add), /read-only for reference docs (cache-friendly), --no-git for unversioned dirs, a symlink for one stray file, or running aider from a shared parent directory.
